heroLead: Follansbee grew up around its steel mill on the Ohio River, and the mineral rights under and around town carry the same industrial-versus-agricultural split found throughout Brooke County.
intro: Land near the mill was largely sold outright for industrial use, but the farmland behind town, further from the river, kept its mineral rights with the original owning families far more often. Follansbee's mineral history is really two separate stories depending on which part of the tract you're tracing.

We buy mineral and royalty interests around Follansbee directly, confirming whether your family's tract sits in the industrial corridor or the surrounding farmland before evaluating its lease and unit status.

sections.heading: River corridor versus farmland ownership
paragraphs: Tracts closer to the mill and the river frequently changed hands for industrial development, sometimes with minerals reserved by the seller and sometimes conveyed outright. Tracts further from the river tend to carry a cleaner, single-family ownership history stretching back generations.

sections.heading: Deep Utica leasing in the Northern Panhandle
paragraphs: Brooke County has drawn operator interest targeting Utica and Point Pleasant rock, and Follansbee-area tracts, particularly the farmland further from the mill, have seen leasing activity layered over any older shallow-well leases already on file.

sections.heading: Confirming your interest before we price it
paragraphs: We pull the recorded deed and lease history for your specific Follansbee-area tract at the Brooke County Courthouse before making an offer, since the industrial and agricultural halves of town have genuinely different ownership patterns.

That distinction shows up most clearly when a family remembers land near the mill being sold generations ago but isn't sure whether the mineral rights went with it. We confirm that one way or the other from the recorded deed rather than leaving it to memory.

faqs.question: My family's land near the mill was sold decades ago. Do we still own the minerals?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the sale reserved mineral rights. We check the specific recorded deed to confirm.

faqs.question: Is there active deep-rights leasing near Follansbee?
faqs.answer: It varies by tract. We check current lease and unit records covering Utica and Point Pleasant rights for your specific tract.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my tract is near the river or further out in the farmland?
faqs.answer: It can affect the ownership history and current leasing status, which is why we evaluate each tract on its own recorded terms.

faqs.question: How do I find out which pattern applies to my family's Follansbee-area tract?
faqs.answer: We locate the recorded deed history for your specific tract through the Brooke County Clerk's office and confirm which pattern applies before making an offer.
